theorem spec_main_rel_iff (N : Fin 5 → ℚ) (t : ℚ) :
    ValRel (getEx (specLib I cstar ell T c3 Nc) 3) (List.ofFn N ++ [t]) ↔
      ∃ K : Fin 5 → ℚ,
        ValRel (getEx (specLib I cstar ell T c3 Nc) 2) (List.ofFn N ++ (List.ofFn K ++ [t])) ∧
        (valueTestTemplate I cstar ell T).Rel (Fin.append (Fin.append N K) ![t]) := by

verdicts.summary: [N] nasqret/z-in-q-lean states a different claim; neither implies the other (differs).
evidence: main_iff relates N,t through valueTestTemplate at shift k, scalarTemplate m from k to K', and CloseAt at K'. It has no exceptional branches and concludes N=iota n, t=n, n not in C, under hM, ndep's PC and a uniform height hypothesis with constant m. [M]'s Val uses the same K in both calls, includes the six exceptional branches and has the full graph t=n. The exceptions appear only later, in integer_polynomial_of_height_and_rank's projected polynomial (exceptional * P), and grep finds no use of value_relation_iff in [N].

main_iff's left side is a different relation (valueTest at kappa, scalarTemplate m linking to K', CloseAt at m*kappa, no exceptional disjuncts) under hM, ndep PC and a uniform height hypothesis, concluding N = iota n, t = n, n not in C; exceptions are only added later at the t-level in integer_polynomial_of_height_and_rank, and value_relation_iff is not used by [N].
